title: Hotel-Signed Days-in-Country Proofs for Remote Teams
one_liner: Hotels and co-living spaces issue signed, privacy-minimal 'nights in this country' attestations, so employers can prove where remote staff worked without tracking their phones.
customer: Finance, tax or mobility leads at remote-first companies of 30-500 staff that run 'work from anywhere' weeks. Secondary payers are co-living operators and boutique hotels that want a 'workation-verified' badge.
problem: A few weeks abroad can create payroll, social-security and permanent-establishment exposure, and employers need day counts to defend their position. In the EU, GPS or phone tracking of staff is legally toxic (GDPR proportionality, works councils), so companies rely on self-reported spreadsheets. The EU Entry/Exit System has logged border crossings automatically since April 2026, yet neither traveler nor employer gets that data in a usable form. 40+ nomad-visa regimes each have different thresholds.
solution: A thin layer on top of hotel and co-living check-in. At checkout the guest opts in, and the property issues a signed attestation (country, region, date range, licence ID, guest name and nothing else) into the traveler's wallet. The employer's HR or tax tool ingests it by CSV or API, and a country rules pack warns when a threshold is near. The MVP needs no integration: a web form, a signed PDF with a QR code, and a shared ledger template.
why_now: EES has been fully live since 10 Apr 2026, so stays are now machine-tracked at the border but invisible to employers. ETIAS slipping to 2027 keeps the friction alive. Hybrid and workation policies have matured, and 40+ nomad visas make cross-border patchwork the norm.
revenue_model: The employer pays about $6 per attestation or $10 per employee per year for the ledger and rules pack. The property pays about $49 a month for a verified listing in a 'workation-ready' directory. Tax advisers can resell it.
non_obvious_insight: Employers cannot lawfully surveil location, but hospitality already produces third-party presence records by law (guest registration and folios). The missing piece is a consent-based export, so the evidence sits in the hotel and not on the phone.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 co-living spaces and boutique hotels (Lisbon, Canaries, Split, Tbilisi) through operator communities. Have one cross-border tax adviser review a one-page attestation spec. Issue attestations by hand. Pitch 5 remote-first startups through their payroll and tax advisers at a $500 pilot, and count first revenue when the first ledger is delivered.

title: Independent Inspections for AI-Built Software
one_liner: A third-party inspection-and-certificate service, staffed by displaced senior engineers, that tells buyers, lenders and insurers what is really inside AI-generated apps before money changes hands.
customer: Buyers of micro-SaaS and small apps on acquisition marketplaces (deals $20k-$2M), SMBs whose apps were built by vibe-coding freelancers, seed investors doing diligence and lenders financing software purchases.
problem: Insiders say AI made software cheap, but the cost moved to trust. Marketplaces are filling with prompt-built products of unknown security, licensing and maintainability, and misconfigured database rules in AI-generated apps have been reported. Traditional code audits cost $10-50k and take weeks. Meanwhile senior devs sit unemployed for many months.
solution: A fixed-price 48-hour 'app inspection': automated scans (secrets, dependency licences, database access rules, auth and PII flows) plus a 2-4 hour senior human review. The output is a standardised graded report like a home-inspection report, with repair-cost estimates and a maintainability score. Inspectors are paid $500-900 each, and an optional badge can be accepted by escrow agents.
why_now: The vibe-coding boom in 2025-26 flooded acquisition marketplaces with AI-built listings, agentic scanners make the first pass nearly free, and unemployed senior engineers are abundant.
revenue_model: $1.5-4k per inspection at 40-50% gross margin, recurring contracts with portfolio buyers, and referral fees from repair shops.
non_obvious_insight: When production cost collapses, value shifts to attestation. Every asset that became cheap to produce (1970s housing, used cars, diamonds) spawned an independent inspector class. Nobody has yet set the trusted standard for AI-built software, and the inspectors' seniority is the moat, the same people the market calls redundant.
first_30_days: Offer discounted $500 inspections in acquisition-marketplace buyer forums and Indie Hackers. Recruit 6 laid-off senior engineers and run 10 inspections on live listings. Publish anonymised findings ('7 of 10 exposed user data') and sign one escrow or broker referral partner.

title: AI Shuttle Mediation for Estranged Families
one_liner: Each estranged party talks privately with an AI that drafts consensus 'bridge' statements and safe first-contact messages, leading to a human-mediated reunion within six weeks.
customer: Estranged adult children and parents (about a quarter of US adults report estrangement from a relative), paying $300-600 per participant, plus elder-law firms and hospital social workers paying $1-3k per reconnection case.
problem: Estrangement is common, painful and costly (unrepresented elders, contested estates), and the first contact is where reconciliation dies because neither side wants to go first. Coaches cost $150 an hour or more, and both parties rarely agree to therapy together.
solution: A structured program. A safety screen excludes abuse cases. Each party completes private AI-guided sessions to articulate needs and non-negotiables. A consensus engine produces candidate bridge statements that both sides rate independently. The first-contact letter or call is scripted and rehearsed in role-play. It ends with a human-mediated 90-minute conversation.
why_now: DeepMind's 2024 'Habermas Machine' showed LLM mediators can find statements groups prefer over human mediators. 2026 voice models handle emotionally sensitive role-play. Estrangement is now widely discussed, and aging and estate systems increasingly hit its costs.
revenue_model: Per-party program fee, B2B per-case fees from elder-law firms and hospitals, and success bonuses.
non_obvious_insight: Reconciliation fails on asymmetric readiness: one side is ready and the other is not. An AI that can shuttle privately with each side at zero social cost solves 'who goes first', which is the real blocker.
first_30_days: Partner with two family-therapist mediators. Recruit 20 pilot participants from estrangement support communities at $300 each. Measure first-contact and second-conversation rates, then approach five elder-law firms with the results.

title: Passive-Radar Drone Detection for Prisons
one_liner: Detect small drones by listening to ambient cell, broadcast and Wi-Fi signals, with no transmitter, no license and no radar permit.
customer: State departments of corrections, county jails, and secondary customers such as critical infrastructure and stadiums.
problem: Cape Canaveral radars see aircraft up to a 747 but not a quadcopter. State prisons face contraband drops with low budgets and cannot deploy active radar or jammers. Remote ID and RF detection miss drones that are not broadcasting.
solution: A rooftop kit of low-cost software-defined radios using the signal reflections of existing cell towers and broadcast transmitters, with ML-based detection of small-drone Doppler signatures. It alerts a mobile app and logs evidence for prosecution, and it is passive so legal risk is minimal.
why_now: Cheap SDRs and modern ML make passive sensing of low-cross-section targets feasible in 2025-26. Small-drone detection is now flagged as thin even at major federal sites, and drone traffic is exploding with 200,000-unit purchases (verify feasibility and prison contraband scale).
revenue_model: $25-60K per site installation plus $500-1,500 per month for software and monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Passivity is the business model. Local agencies cannot legally emit RF or mitigate, so a purely receiving sensor is the only kind they can buy without federal permission.
first_30_days: Recruit one university RF lab. Pilot on a rooftop with an existing tower nearby and log real drone passes. Approach 3 state corrections security chiefs for a paid pilot.

title: Verified-Offer Shield Against H-2A Recruitment Scams
one_liner: A WhatsApp-native registry where growers publish verifiable H-2A job offers and authorized recruiters, so workers can check any offer in seconds and growers get proof they never sanctioned a fee-charging middleman.
customer: Grower associations and large H-2A employers, plus farm labor contractors running H-2A programs, who pay per worker. Workers use it free.
problem: H-2A is scaling as the domestic workforce shrinks (over 300K visas in 2024; EPI expects growth toward 500K jobs after the Oct 2025 wage rule; the workforce reportedly fell by at least 155,000). Fake recruiters and impersonated grower pages sell nonexistent jobs or charge illegal fees. H-2A rules make employers contractually responsible for banning recruiter fees, so a scam in a grower's name is a compliance and reputation hit. Late or absent arrivals mean unharvested crops.
solution: Growers verify their business identity once, attach a DOL job-order number and issue a signed offer card with a QR and short code. Recruiters receive a 'licensed by grower' credential. A worker-side WhatsApp and SMS bot works in Spanish and through voice notes for Indigenous-language speakers (Mixtec, K'iche'). It replies 'verified', 'not found' or 'fee reported' and takes fee complaints. Growers get an audit trail of their recruiter chain and arrival tracking.
why_now: The immigration crackdown removed workers, and strawberry and almond growers reportedly lost up to 30% of crews in early 2026. The H-2A wage rule changed the incentives. AI makes fake job pages, voices and documents cheap. WhatsApp Business APIs are mature, and nobody in agriculture has a verification layer.
revenue_model: $15-40 per worker per season paid by the employer or association, a premium tier for recruiter-chain audit trails and DOL-ready records, and possible lender or insurer sponsorship.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the grower, not the victim. Growers carry the legal and commercial exposure to recruiter fraud and have the budget, while workers cannot pay. Verification for the poor is funded by the party with compliance liability.
first_30_days: Sign one grower association for a pilot with 3 member farms. Build the WhatsApp bot on the Meta Cloud API. Recruit 2-3 recruiter partners in Mexico and Guatemala. Collect 20 real scam examples through worker centers and legal-aid groups, and use them to demonstrate detection.

title: Operating System For Staff Cooperatives
one_liner: Digitise the exercise-book ledgers of workplace cooperatives, which are the cheapest credit pipe for Nigerian civil servants and teachers, then connect their idle surpluses to each other.
customer: Thrift-and-credit cooperative societies for teachers, nurses, civil servants, police, university staff and market associations. Their executive committees pay for the software. Later, the MFB or bank partner that funds wholesale lending between cooperatives.
problem: Outsiders assume Nigerian salary earners borrow from loan apps or MFBs. In reality a huge share borrow from staff cooperatives at about 10% flat per year, with payroll check-off giving near-zero defaults. But most societies run on Excel, exercise books and a treasurer's WhatsApp. Collapses come from embezzlement, unreconciled employer remittances, and members who cannot see their balances. Some cooperatives sit on idle surplus at 3-8% in a savings account while others in the same city ration loans to a waiting list.
solution: A WhatsApp-first ledger and treasury app: member savings and shares, loan applications with digital guarantors, approval workflows, automated reconciliation of employer check-off remittances against the deduction schedule, monthly member statements, and AGM voting and dividends. AI vision digitises the old exercise books on day one from phone photos. Once ledgers are clean and trusted, add an inter-cooperative wholesale line, routed through a bank or MFB partner, where surplus societies lend to constrained ones at a spread.
why_now: Multimodal AI can now read handwritten ledgers cheaply and reliably, which removes the onboarding barrier that killed earlier software. Tighter FCCPC rules on digital lenders have thinned out predatory apps and pushed members back toward cooperatives. Inflation and salary delays have raised demand for member loans. Open banking and cheaper payout APIs let cooperatives collect and disburse without paper cheques.
revenue_model: SaaS of about N25k-100k per month per cooperative, or N100-200 per member per month. A 0.5-1% spread on inter-cooperative wholesale loans. Fees on embedded products for members (insurance, school-fee financing, phones and gadgets) via the platform.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not capital or customers but trusted records. Once a cooperative's ledger is clean and independent, it becomes a credit-bearing entity and its members can become a distribution channel, which is why the software is a wedge into wholesale lending. The check-off arrangement with the employer is the underwriting moat that no fintech can replicate.
first_30_days: Approach 10 cooperatives through teachers' unions, hospital staff associations and state civil-service networks. Digitise their books free using photo OCR, then start charging from month two. Get an accountant or cooperative-federation officer as a paid advisor for credibility. Track the first reconciliation win, such as finding a missing month of employer remittance, and use it as the case study.

title: Human Concierge for Phone-Free Adults
one_liner: A $29 per month phone number staffed by humans who handle the app-only chores of modern life (QR menus, parking, rides, boarding passes, 2FA migration) so people can keep their dumbphone.
customer: Adults 25-55 who switched to flip phones, a Light Phone or a stripped-down iPhone, or want to but keep failing; first found in dumbphone communities and among buyers of minimalist phone brands, then tech workers and parents who go phone-free alongside their teens.
problem: People do not abandon dumbphones from lack of willpower but from friction: authenticator-only two-factor logins, QR-code menus, parking and transit apps, rideshare, mobile boarding passes and app-only bank features. Then they buy the smartphone back. Device makers respond by adding features (cameras, maps, apps), which recreates the problem. As the flip-phone revival hits the mainstream in 2026, the failure rate is the business opportunity.
solution: Two products. First, a one-time 'Switch Day' ($99): a human sits with the customer for two hours, ports the number, migrates 2FA away from authenticator apps to hardware keys, voice codes or email, moves bank alerts to text and voice, prints backup codes and paper maps. Second, 'the Desk', a call/text line staffed by humans with a company smartphone and virtual cards: they book the ride to your address, pay the parking zone by plate, read you the QR menu, print or hand over the boarding pass, and make the reservation that only exists in an app. Fair-use unlimited requests on the subscription, with pay-per-errand for heavier tasks.
why_now: The dumbphone and analog movement hit mainstream press in 2026 (Fortune's Gen Z analog coverage in February, new flip-phone startups launching in September), while schools in about 40 states now restrict phones, pushing parents to model the behavior. Meanwhile, essential services keep going app-only. Cheap voice and workflow tools let a small human team serve dozens of subscribers per agent.
revenue_model: $29 per month subscription, $99 Switch Day setup fee, bundle and referral deals with dumbphone makers (a Desk membership included with each device), employer perk for 'focus' or wellness programs, and per-errand fees for premium requests.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce product in the anti-screen economy is not another device but human proxies for the smartphone-shaped holes in society. The business grows every time a restaurant or city makes something QR-only, and every new mandate is a marketing lead. Abstainers are also a tight, vocal community, so each retained customer is an ambassador, and the manufacturers gain from a service that reduces returns.
first_30_days: Offer 20 people in dumbphone communities a free Switch Day in exchange for interviews and permission to log every request. Run the Desk by hand from one shared iPhone, a Google Voice number and an Airtable. Categorize the first 300 requests to find the top 10 that drive 80% of the pain. Convert users to $29 per month and approach two minimalist phone brands about bundling. Target 100 paying members by month 5.

title: Cross-Border Income Passport for Freelancers
one_liner: Give stablecoin-paid remote workers a verifiable, portable income record that landlords, lenders and visa agents accept.
customer: Freelancers and remote workers in Nigeria, the Philippines, Colombia and Kenya; landlords, lenders and visa agents pay to verify.
problem: Freelancers cannot get portable income records for loans or visas, and stablecoin and platform-wallet earnings leave no bank paper trail.
solution: Connect wallets, payout platforms and invoices, then produce signed income attestations with a QR verification link. The wedge is rental and visa income letters at about $15 each for remote workers in Lagos and Manila.
why_now: Stablecoin payroll and invoicing tools like Bloccpay are spreading, Flutterwave and Yellow Card are scaling, and LatAm lenders are hunting for new borrowers.
revenue_model: $10-20 per attestation, plus $1-3 per verification call from lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in stablecoin income is proving it, not moving it. Whoever gets accepted by three lenders becomes a bureau for the remote-work diaspora.
first_30_days: Build attestations from Payoneer, Wise and USDC statements and test with 50 workers and one landlord network.

title: Dixie Flatline for Retiring Plant Operators
one_liner: Neuromancer's Dixie Flatline (a dead expert preserved as a consultable construct) built for retiring water and plant operators, with consent, clip-grounded answers and royalties paid to the expert.
customer: Municipal water and wastewater utilities, rural electric co-ops and small chemical or food plants, reached through state rural water associations and funded by state workforce and infrastructure grants.
problem: A large share of plant operators is nearing retirement, and the knowledge that matters is tacit ('when pump 3 hums like that in the cold, do this'). SOP binders miss it, experts sandbag because they fear being replaced, and a hallucinating chatbot is unacceptable when chlorine dosing is involved.
solution: A three-week Walkdown Capture: the expert tours the plant with a chest camera and mic, thinking aloud. Their answers are aligned with SCADA and alarm history so past incidents can be replayed ('what did you do in the January freeze?'). Structured critical-decision interviews feed a queryable construct that answers only with citations to the expert's own clips, deployed on a tablet or radio for night operators. The retiree signs a consent and royalty agreement, is paid per consult, can revoke, and remains reachable as a paid human escalation.
why_now: Utilities are in the middle of a retirement wave, and cheap wearable cameras, speech-to-text and retrieval systems make capture-and-query affordable for a small team. Regulators and grant programs increasingly fund workforce succession.
revenue_model: $20-45k per capture project, $1-3k per month hosting per plant, and a royalty share passed through to the expert.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not modeling but eliciting and compensating. Experts hide knowledge when the goal is replacement, and paying them a revocable royalty flips the incentive. Grounding every answer in the expert's own clips solves the hallucination problem and makes the tool defensible with regulators and insurers.
first_30_days: Ask three state rural water associations for introductions. Run one pilot with a retiring operator for $5k or free, and produce a short demo of a construct answering a night-shift question with clip evidence. Aim for three paid projects by month six.

title: Rural Vet Call Logs as Outbreak Early Warning
one_liner: Producers call the vet before they call the state. Anonymized weekly counts of abortions, maggot wounds, sudden deaths and respiratory clusters are a leading indicator that traders, insurers and packers will pay for.
customer: Buyers: cattle and feeder analytics desks, market advisory and commodity funds, packer and feedlot risk managers, livestock and dairy insurers or reinsurers, animal health company territory teams, and state animal health boards (contracts or grants). Suppliers are participating rural vets, who get free early regional alerts and a small revenue share.
problem: Official disease data lags by weeks because it waits on lab confirmation, and ranchers hesitate to report to the state because a quarantine costs them money. Screwworm was confirmed in a Texas calf in June 2026 after roughly 60 years without a US case, and H5N1 in dairy cattle was spreading for months before detection in 2024. Cattle futures at record prices with a 70-year low herd move violently on rumor, and nobody has a systematic ground-level feed.
solution: A 30-second end-of-week SMS or one-tap tally where each vet reports counts by syndrome (abortion clusters, navel or wound maggots, sudden deaths, neurological, respiratory, milk drops) and ZIP3 or county. Counts are aggregated with k-anonymity (no client identity, minimum practice thresholds) and compared to seasonal baselines. Outputs are a weekly 'Rural Vet Pulse' regional index, push alerts when a region deviates, and an API for institutional subscribers. Vets get the regional alerts free, which is the give-to-get hook.
why_now: New World screwworm has been confirmed in Texas and New Mexico since June 2026, with the first infested horse reported in September 2026, and movement restrictions plus sterile-fly shortages make the outbreak's trajectory the biggest driver of cattle risk. H5N1 in dairy is ongoing, federal animal health staffing is stretched, and academic syndromic surveillance systems exist in Europe (Netherlands, France, Great Britain) but I found no commercial equivalent built from US rural vet practices.
revenue_model: $2-10K per month per institutional data subscriber (analytics desks, insurers, packers), enterprise API tiers, sponsored regional alerts from animal health companies, state or regional government pilots, and a $100-300 per month revenue share to each contributing practice.
non_obvious_insight: Ranchers under-report to the state because reporting costs them money, but they do not hide problems from their vet because they need the vet's drugs and help. The vet's phone is the earliest sensor in the system, and vets cannot share client data but can share counts. Contrarian point: the absence of calls is also a signal, because call volume drops when producers hide problems during a quarantine.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 large-animal practices in Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Kansas and Nebraska through state VMA lists and large-animal vet Facebook groups. Build the weekly tally as a plain SMS survey, with no software integration. Publish a free regional weekly newsletter to the vets as the hook. Backtest screwworm lead time against USDA confirmation dates and pitch 3 market-advisory or cattle analytics shops for a $1-2K per month paid pilot.

title: Pay Farmers to Under-Irrigate, Not Fallow
one_liner: A broker and satellite-verification layer that pays growers of alfalfa, hay and cotton for mid-season deficit irrigation and hands corporate and municipal buyers audited acre-feet.
customer: Buyers: corporate water coalitions (Amazon put $20M into the Water Resilience Coalition's Colorado River effort, $32M raised toward a $100M goal) and Lower Basin cities and water agencies. Sellers: irrigation districts and forage/annual-crop growers. The buyer pays.
problem: The 2027-2036 Colorado River framework pushes cuts onto agriculture (about 70% of the river), yet corporate money has no settlement layer. Fallowing is politically toxic and guts farm income. Drip and efficiency upgrades often do not reduce consumptive use, so nobody can say what a verified acre-foot is.
solution: A standard split-season contract. The grower skips the last irrigation cycles, or accepts deficit irrigation at pre-agreed growth stages. Consumptive use is measured by satellite ET (an OpenET-style ensemble) against a five-year baseline and paired control fields. Payment is escrowed per verified acre-foot, and the buyer gets a basin-and-year-tagged certificate. Wedge product: one district pilot plus a buyer dashboard. Federal credit is not needed to start, so begin with districts that already hold Reclamation conservation agreements.
why_now: The Aug 2026 Record of Decision fixed the 2027-2036 rules. Powell plus Mead storage is about 36% of capacity, the lowest since before Glen Canyon Dam filled. Corporate money is arriving, and open ET datasets are now good enough to audit individual fields.
revenue_model: 10-15% spread on each acre-foot transaction (roughly $40-90 on a $400-600/af price), plus $20-50k/yr verification SaaS to districts.
non_obvious_insight: Only cuts in consumptive use create basin-level savings, and forage crops tolerate a mid-season deficit far better than farm economies tolerate fallowed fields. Buyers are really paying for measurement certainty, so whoever owns the audit trail sets the price and the standard.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: run retrospective ET for 10 alfalfa/hay growers in one Lower Basin or Grand Valley district (public data, free tier) and price the acre-feet they could offer. Days 10-25: build a one-page buyer pitch and dashboard mock. Days 25-30: pitch the Water Resilience Coalition and two city water agencies to underwrite a 500-1,000 af pilot for the 2027 season, since contracts get negotiated over winter.

title: Blind Spend Tokens for Secretive Buyer Agents
one_liner: A buyer-side privacy gateway that lets agents pay for data and APIs with unlinkable tokens that prove 'authorized and funded' without revealing who is asking, what the price ceiling is, or what the question was.
customer: Buy-side and R&D organizations whose queries are the secret: hedge funds and asset managers, pharma competitive-intelligence and BD teams, M&A law firms and defense contractors that route agents to paid data, patent, expert-network and search APIs.
problem: Agent commerce protocols hand the seller the buyer's leverage by design. Signed mandates state a maximum price and intent, agent IDs let vendors profile and price-discriminate, and the queries themselves (a ticker, a compound, a patent family) reveal research direction. Query logs can leak, be resold or be front-run.
solution: A gateway sitting between the buyer's agents and vendors. Blind-signed, unlinkable spend tokens (Privacy Pass style) are issued after KYC by a bank or escrow, so the vendor is guaranteed payment but cannot identify the buyer. Mandates are committed and proven within cap using a zero-knowledge range proof or a TEE mediator, so the ceiling is never disclosed. Queries are batched, cached and mixed with decoys across a pooled anonymity set of customers.
why_now: Signed-agent identity and KYA schemes are proliferating across card networks and web standards, all oriented toward reassuring sellers. Privacy Pass is now a set of IETF standards. Agents issue thousands of paid queries per day, so leakage volume has exploded.
revenue_model: $8-25k per month per firm plus 0.5-1% of pass-through spend. A one-time $15k query-leakage audit is the entry product.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is building 'know your agent' for the seller's benefit. The buyer's reservation price and research intent are the real assets, and privacy for the buyer is unclaimed territory. For funds, leaked query patterns are alpha decay, which gives a hard-dollar budget line. The chicken-and-egg problem of anonymity sets is solved by starting with decoy traffic and TEE-operated pooling.
first_30_days: Sell 5 query-leakage audits ($15k each) to funds and pharma CI teams: instrument what their agents leak to vendors (headers, mandates, IPs, query text) and deliver a report. Turn the audit findings into a decoy-plus-proxy gateway for the three data vendors most used by early customers.

title: Stablecoin Depeg and Freeze Cover
one_liner: GENIUS made stablecoins legal, not insured. Sell corporate treasurers parametric cover for issuer depeg, redemption suspension and wallet freezes so their risk committees will approve holding balances.
customer: Treasurers and CFOs at mid-market and payments companies holding $1M-$100M in USDC or USDT, including corporate clients of the new Citi and Coinbase flow.
problem: GENIUS gives holders priority claims but no deposit insurance. USDT is about $140B and USDC about $74B, the Senate Democrats' Tether report alleges $2B of Iranian flows against $550M frozen, and Bitcoin has drawn down about 50%. Auditors and risk committees want risk transfer, and there is none.
solution: Parametric cover that pays when a named stablecoin trades below a threshold (for example $0.985) for 72 hours on defined venues, when redemption is suspended beyond a set number of days, or when the issuer freezes the insured's wallets. Price from on-chain and reserve-attestation data and place capital with crypto-native and traditional ILS providers through an MGA.
why_now: Corporate flows went live on 2026-09-28. The Fed proposed reserve and capital rules on 2026-09-24, making issuer risk legible. Annual volume is over $90T, and softening reinsurance gives capital a reason to look at new risks.
revenue_model: Premium of about 0.3-1.0% of covered balance per year, MGA commission, and a paid reserve-monitoring and rating subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume regulated equals safe, but corporate risk committees need transferred risk, not comfort. The trigger is objective and cheap to verify, and an independent reserve monitor and rating is a valuable by-product.
first_30_days: Publish a public reserve and peg-monitoring dashboard as a lead magnet and pitch 20 treasurers. Negotiate a first $10M of quota-share capacity from a crypto-native capital provider and pilot with a payments company holding customer float.

title: Josephine Reborn: Permit Concierge for Home Kitchens
one_liner: Josephine's home-cooked-meal marketplace was boxed in by health law; California's MEHKO law now licenses home restaurants, so build the permit concierge and a compliant direct-to-consumer storefront, not another marketplace.
customer: Home cooks, especially immigrant and regional-cuisine specialists (tamales, Armenian, Korean, Oaxacan, Filipino), in Los Angeles County and the roughly 19 California jurisdictions that had authorized MEHKOs as of May 2026. Many already sell via Instagram and WhatsApp without a permit.
problem: MEHKO caps are 30 meals/day, 90/week and roughly $107k/year. Applying costs about $597 plus about $347/yr in LA County, plus food-handler certification, menu SOPs, labels, sales logs and inspections. Third-party delivery apps are restricted, so cooks cannot just list on DoorDash. No tool enforces the caps, produces inspector-ready records, or helps neighbors find them, and paperwork is mostly in English.
solution: A permit concierge ($249-399 one-time) that completes the application, SOPs and multilingual allergen labels. Then a $20/mo cook operating system: link-in-bio storefront with pre-orders and pickup windows, automatic sell-out at 30/day and 90/week, temperature and sales logs exported in the county's format, and Stripe payments. Demand comes from neighborhood 'Friday drop' maps and newsletters and workplace pickup clusters. Cooks own their customers; there is no marketplace.
why_now: MEHKO adoption is spreading county by county (17 counties plus Berkeley and Long Beach by May 2026), with LA County running an active program. Restaurant prices are high, social commerce is normal, and AI makes multilingual SOPs and labels nearly free. A few early MEHKO startups exist, so the opening is to be permit-first, multilingual and neighborhood-by-neighborhood.
revenue_model: $249-399 permit concierge fee; $20/mo per cook SaaS; roughly 1% payments margin; affiliate income from food-handler training and liability insurance. Later, a bulk-permitting contract with counties that want cleaner inspection records.
non_obvious_insight: The marketplace was the illegal or unscalable part, and under MEHKO it is structurally limited to direct-to-consumer sales. The scarce asset is the permit, and the winning product is compliance and storefront tooling that turns each cook into her own licensed restaurant. Enforcing the meal caps in software becomes a feature, and it makes the vendor the county health department's preferred partner.
first_30_days: Attend LA County MEHKO office hours. Find 10 cooks on Instagram (#lahomecook, #tamales) and do their applications free in exchange for case studies. Build the storefront with Shopify or Stripe plus a no-code cap rule. Target 5 issued permits within about 60 days, then start charging the $20/mo.

title: Camera-Free Nap-Room Proof-of-Supervision
one_liner: Start with NFC crib tags that create tamper-evident safe-sleep check logs for childcare centers, then add 60GHz radar that verifies presence and breathing without any camera.
customer: Childcare centers' infant and toddler rooms, small chains, childcare liability insurers and brokers, and licensing agencies.
problem: Safe-sleep checks are handwritten logs that can be filled in after the fact. Sleep supervision failures drive licensing violations, insurance claims and tragedies. Cameras raise privacy objections. After abuse incidents at premium chains (Bright Horizons NYC, per the brief), parents and insurers want proof that supervision happened, not just cameras.
solution: Phase 1: teachers tap a badge on an NFC tag at each crib every interval, producing a timestamped, tamper-evident log and alerts for missed checks. Phase 2: a ceiling-mounted mmWave radar puck detects presence, motion and position class with no images, cross-checking the log. Positioned as compliance logging, not a medical device.
why_now: Low-cost 60GHz radar chips and infant-sensing research are now mature. Insurers are tightening abuse and molestation coverage (from memory). Public attention to childcare safety is high after the 2025-26 incidents.
revenue_model: $20-45 per crib per month plus a $150 radar device, with insurer premium-credit revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: The value is proof of supervision, not detection. Detection claims invite FDA regulation and false-assurance liability, while insurers and inspectors will pay for un-fakeable evidence that checks happened.
first_30_days: Build the NFC tag and phone app. Pilot in 3 infant rooms. Talk to 2 childcare insurers or brokers about premium credits. Prototype breathing detection on an evaluation radar board with adult volunteers and a manikin, never infants.

title: Loss-Draft Concierge for Disaster Rebuilds
one_liner: A draw desk that gets the insurance money for a destroyed house out of the mortgage servicer's restricted account and into the rebuild, paid by the contractors who need cash to start.
customer: Mortgaged homeowners whose houses were destroyed or damaged by fire, flood or storm pay $1,500-3,000 flat or about 1% of proceeds. Rebuild contractors pay 1.5-2.5% of each accelerated draw.
problem: When a mortgaged house is destroyed, insurance checks are made out to both the owner and the servicer. The servicer parks the money in a loss-draft account and releases it in inspection-gated stages, each requiring a contract, contractor license proof, permits, lien waivers, W-9s and photos. Homeowners cannot assemble the packet. Contractors will not start without money. Families pay rent and a mortgage on a lot with nothing on it. Rebuild fraud thrives in the gap.
solution: A draw desk that takes the servicer's letter and builds the draw packet in the exact format the servicer wants. It verifies the contractor's license, collects conditional and unconditional lien waivers on the state statutory forms, books inspections, submits, and chases weekly. It escalates to servicer executive complaint lines and state regulators. It ties every disbursement to milestone photos and waivers so the homeowner is protected from paying for work not done. It never holds the funds, which avoids money-transmitter issues. Later add bridge financing against expected draws.
why_now: The January 2025 Los Angeles fires destroyed roughly 16,000 structures and rebuilds are now at peak permit and construction paperwork. Storm and flood rebuilds continue in Texas, North Carolina and Florida, and every season adds more. Additional-living-expense coverage has clocks that expire, which makes delay costly. AI document handling makes lien-waiver, permit and inspection-photo checks cheap for a small team.
revenue_model: Flat rebuild-admin package or about 1% of proceeds from homeowners. A per-draw acceleration fee of 1.5-2.5% from contractors. Later, a spread on bridge loans and referral revenue from lenders and builders.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not the insurer. The money already exists and is locked behind paperwork the homeowner cannot produce. Public adjusters take about 10% to fight the insurer but nobody specializes in this second fight. The hidden buyer is the contractor, whose cash flow decides whether the site ever starts.
first_30_days: Join fire-survivor community groups and rebuild nonprofits in one affected area. Offer a free draw-packet review to the first 10 households. Sign 3 rebuild contractors whose draws are stalled. Charge a flat fee only after the first draw is released. Document days-to-funds before and after as your proof, then take the case studies to the next disaster market.

title: Certified Coder Audit Pods for Autonomous Coding
one_liner: Displaced medical coders, organised as credentialed audit pods, provide the sampled human sign-off that lets hospitals trust autonomous coding AI to submit claims.
customer: Autonomous medical-coding vendors who need a human audit layer to close hospital deals, hospital revenue-cycle compliance leaders and physician groups. Pricing is $1.5-4 per audited chart or $15-40k a month per pod.
problem: Coding is a highly exposed white-collar job, and coders are being cut as autonomous coding reaches production. But billing compliance (False Claims Act exposure, payer and RAC audits) needs accountable, credentialed review. Vendors' own audit teams are thin or offshore and unlicensed.
solution: Pods of 5-10 CPC/CCS-certified ex-coders with a lead auditor, receiving risk-stratified samples of AI-coded charts via API. They provide error-taxonomy dashboards, monthly compliance attestations, feedback loops that retrain the model and contractual accuracy thresholds.
why_now: Autonomous coding moved into production in 2025-26, the coder job pool is shrinking, payers are using AI audits themselves and hospital margins are under pressure.
revenue_model: Per-chart fees or pod retainers at 45-55% gross margin, plus premium attestation packages.
non_obvious_insight: Full automation in healthcare billing stalls at the accountability signature, and the people displaced are the ones who can provide it. The human role shifts from doing to auditing a 5-10% sample, which is recurring compliance spend rather than labor cost. The audit data is also valuable training data for the vendor.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 laid-off certified coders through AAPC and AHIMA forums. Pitch 5 autonomous-coding startups a pilot: audit 1,000 charts at about $2 each with a written accuracy report. Sign one as a design partner.

title: N-of-1 Trial Network for the Peptide Boom
one_liner: IRB-supervised, blinded, randomized N-of-1 trials that let peptide users learn what works for them while building the missing evidence base.
customer: Consumers already using or considering BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu or KPV (pay ~$249 per 12-week trial), plus clinics, 503A pharmacies, wearable and supplement brands that need substantiation.
problem: Peptides are legal-ish again (HHS Feb 2026; FDA panel Jul 23, 2026 backed BPC-157 and KPV despite agency concerns), yet there is no evidence base. Users self-experiment uncontrolled, clinics cannot substantiate claims, and the FDA panel itself flagged the gaps.
solution: A 503A pharmacy ships coded vials (active vs placebo, randomized crossover), an app collects pre-registered endpoints (pain scores, sleep, grip strength, wearable HRV) plus baseline and 8-week safety labs, and Bayesian analysis returns each person's answer and contributes to a public aggregated dataset. Start with BPC-157 for tendon and joint pain.
why_now: Peptide deregulation in 2026, cheap wearables and remote endpoints, AI-assisted protocol design and statistics, and a crowd of volunteers already injecting. N-of-1 designs need tens of people per question, not hundreds.
revenue_model: $249 per participant, $50-150k sponsor-funded studies from clinics and brands, and data licensing.
non_obvious_insight: When regulation retreats, credible evidence becomes the scarce good. The crowd already volunteers, and pre-registered N-of-1 series can outrun a traditional RCT for low-risk, subjective-endpoint questions.
first_30_days: Draft protocol and IRB submission with an FDA IND-exemption determination from counsel. Recruit ~60 people through biohacker communities and one partner clinic. Line up a 503A pharmacy for blinded placebo and open a $249 waitlist for the first cohort.

title: IEP-Ready Adaptive Hardware, Printed to Order
one_liner: A micro-manufacturer that acts as the approved vendor for special-education adaptive hardware, starting with custom AAC keyguards for tablets and expanding to OT-prescribed grips, switch mounts and positioning aids.
customer: School district special-ed and assistive-technology coordinators, school SLPs and OTs, and private pediatric therapy clinics, paid through district purchase orders funded by IEP obligations.
problem: Free keyguard designs exist, and Etsy sellers make standard ones. But an SLP has no time to print, a district can't pay an Etsy seller by purchase order, and a custom AAC grid on a specific tablet and case needs an exact fit. Legally required AT then arrives weeks late. Every tablet or case refresh orphans last year's keyguards.
solution: A catalog and a 48-hour custom service. The SLP uploads a screenshot of the AAC layout and the tablet and case model. We return a fit-verified keyguard with an IEP-friendly quote and invoice. Then expand to OT-prescribed items (pencil grips, adaptive handles, switch and tablet mounts, tactile schedule boards) using a clinician-approved parametric library. Paperwork arrives ready for the file: W-9, liability insurance, net-30 terms and cooperative-purchasing listings.
why_now: Consumer-grade printing is now reliable enough for small runs of durable parts. Tablet-based AAC is now standard practice, and app grid layouts are standardized enough to parametrize. Districts are under pressure to meet AT obligations with tight budgets. Open-source designs prove the demand but leave the procurement gap wide open.
revenue_model: Per item ($35 to $95 for keyguards; $10 to $150 for other adaptive items), plus an annual district 'AT Bench' subscription ($3k to $8k covering a set number of custom items and a design consult).
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing isn't the printing or even the design, since clinicians will share designs for free. It's the procurement wrapper: being a vendor a district can legally and easily pay. Whoever holds 'approved vendor' status with a few purchasing cooperatives gets pulled into every district's AT budget. Print cost is $4 against a $80 to $150 price because the customer is paying for zero-friction compliance and clinical fit.
first_30_days: Take the open-source keyguard parametric files and verify fit against the five most common tablet and case combinations. Post in SLP and AT groups: 'send a screenshot of your layout, first keyguard at cost, PO accepted.' Complete vendor registration with two districts and apply to one purchasing cooperative. Target 15 paid orders and one district relationship.

title: Surety-Bonded License Plates for AI Agents
one_liner: A registrar that binds each autonomous agent to a legally accountable, insured principal through a surety bond and a revocable credential merchants and platforms can check.
customer: Agent developers and vendors that need acceptance by merchants, booking and B2B procurement platforms, the merchants and platforms that want to admit agents safely, and surety insurers or MGAs.
problem: Visa, Mastercard and Amex are activating agent payments in 2026, but dispute and liability infrastructure barely exists. Merchants bear the chargebacks, and Mastercard is reportedly planning scheme-carried liability for certified agents. Identity schemes such as Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol and Cloudflare's signed agents say who an agent is, but not who pays when it misbehaves.
solution: Register the agent and underwrite it with a test suite, spend caps and a behaviour policy. Issue a signed credential with a visible bond limit, and let merchants and platforms verify it with one API call. A claims process pays merchants for agent-caused losses, and violations revoke the credential. Start with an MGA and fronting-carrier partnership.
why_now: Card networks are moving on agent payments in 2026, Lloyd's-backed AI liability covers launched in 2025, and merchants are asking who is liable for agent orders. Signed-agent identity standards exist, so the missing layer is accountability.
revenue_model: Annual premium of 1-5% of bond limit, a registration fee, and float on the claims reserve.
non_obvious_insight: Identity without liability is theatre. The mature trust machine for strangers who might not pay is suretyship (contractor licences, notary bonds), not a reputation score, and a bond turns 'trust me' into a price.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical (restaurant and hotel booking, or B2B procurement agents). Sign five agent developers, secure a letter of intent from a surety or MGA, build the underwriting test suite, and get three merchants to trial a bonded-only allowlist.

title: Pooled Tariff-Surcharge Refund Claims for Small Buyers
one_liner: Connect to small businesses' accounting data, find tariff surcharges they paid distributors, and pool their claims against the same suppliers now receiving IEEPA refunds.
customer: Restaurants and restaurant groups, contractors, small manufacturers and retailers that bought through distributors who added tariff surcharge lines in 2025, paying on contingency.
problem: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, and CBP began taking refund claims through its CAPE portal on April 20, 2026, with roughly $175B owed to about 330,000 importers. Suppliers who passed the tariff through on itemized surcharges are now collecting refunds. Small buyers who paid those lines have claims but no visibility and no lawyer, since a $3k claim is uneconomic to pursue alone.
solution: Read 24 months of AP data (QuickBooks, Bill.com, email invoices) with an LLM to isolate itemized surcharges and post-tariff price jumps by supplier. Aggregate each supplier's small-buyer claims into one pooled demand or arbitration or class action through a partner consumer-protection firm. Track which suppliers have filed for refunds. Later, add econometric analysis of 'embedded' non-itemized price increases.
why_now: Refunds are being issued now (typically 60 to 90 days after acceptance), so the window for suppliers to hold and spend the money is short. Pass-through disputes have begun to appear in courts, but law firms focus on large B2B claimants. Litigation and CBP timing remains uncertain (the government appealed the refund order), which favors moving fast.
revenue_model: 20% to 30% contingency on recovered amounts, plus a fixed fee to run the AP analysis for larger buyers.
non_obvious_insight: Claims are tiny individually but concentrated by supplier. Two hundred restaurants that all bought from the same three distributors are a multimillion-dollar claim against three defendants. The supplier-level dataset (who added surcharges, when, how much, who filed) is the moat, and it is built one small customer at a time.
first_30_days: Build a free 'surcharge finder' that scans an uploaded invoice export or QuickBooks connection and shows what was paid. Recruit through restaurant and contractor associations and bookkeepers. Sign 50 claimants on contingency and target the 10 distributors whose surcharges show up most often. Line up a partner litigation firm.

title: Orphaned Job and Membership Rescue Desk
one_liner: When a PE roll-up of contractors collapses, package its unfinished jobs, prepaid maintenance memberships and warranties and hand them to healthy local contractors, while lenders and trustees get paid for the recovery.
customer: Two payers. (1) Private-credit lenders, Chapter 11 trustees and creditor committees of collapsed home-service platforms, on a success fee. (2) Local independent contractors and newly formed tech-owned shops, who pay a per-customer transfer fee to inherit service obligations and customer relationships.
problem: Roll-ups of HVAC, remodeling and roofing firms are failing, and the stranded parties have no one to coordinate. Homeowners are left with half-finished jobs and prepaid plans. Laid-off technicians hold the customer relationships but not the customer data. Lenders are owed $100M+ from shells with almost no assets and have no operating capability to finish jobs and collect receivables.
solution: A rapid-response playbook plus lightweight software: (1) an intake site for stranded customers ('my contractor shut down'); (2) an import of the estate's job, warranty and membership data from its field-service or CRM exports, scored by job stage, deposit status, and geography; (3) matching to vetted local contractors, with milestone escrow so the deposit follows the work; (4) a lender/trustee dashboard showing completed WIP and recovered receivables. A starter kit (entity formation, insurance, licensing checklist, FSM software setup) lets laid-off technicians become buyers of the books they used to serve.
why_now: 2025 was a record year for PE-linked distress. The PE Stakeholder Project counts PE firms in 19 of the 35 largest US bankruptcies (54%) and 21 of 41 large ones (51%) in 2025, though it is an advocacy source. Bain's 2026 reports say borrowing costs are 8-9% versus 6-7% a decade ago, and deals now need 10-12% annual EBITDA growth to hit target returns. That squeezes leveraged service roll-ups. Private credit, not banks, now holds much of the paper, and these lenders lack turnaround operations for field-service businesses.
revenue_model: 5-10% success fee on WIP completed and receivables recovered for the estate. $150-400 per customer transferred, paid by the acquiring contractor. Optional 1-1.5% escrow fee on consumer deposits. Subscription for lenders who want a watchlist and pre-built playbook.
non_obvious_insight: In a roll-up collapse the valuable asset is the unfulfilled service obligations (prepaid memberships, warranties, half-built jobs), not the brand or customer list. Local independents will pay to inherit them, and lenders recover more from orderly completion than from a liquidation. Renovo, formed in 2021 by Audax by combining three home-remodeling businesses (later seven), filed in November 2025 with about $50,000 in assets against more than $100M in liabilities, after roughly $150M from BlackRock, Apollo and Oaktree. About 1,500 workers were terminated, some without final paychecks, and homeowners were left with incomplete projects. Cutting installer pay from 10-12% to 8% drove out skilled workers (https://pestakeholder.org/private-equity-bankruptcy-tracker/). In September 2026 PE-backed United Air Temp (Littlejohn's United Comfort Group, eight partner companies) filed WARN notices for 135+ layoffs across VA and MD, closing its Lorton HQ effective Nov 10, 2026 (https://www.achrnews.com/articles/166687-private-equity-backed-united-air-temp-announces-mass-layoffs). WARN notices are a free, public lead source for the next rescue.
first_30_days: Build a watchlist from public WARN notices and bankruptcy dockets for home-service platforms. Stand up a 'my contractor shut down' landing page and intake form for one distressed metro. Sign 5 local independent contractors who agree to take transferred customers at a flat fee. Cold-approach restructuring counsel and Chapter 11 trustees at 5-10 private-credit special-situations desks with a free 2-week pilot on a small estate. Estate authority over customer data will be the gating legal step, so line up a bankruptcy attorney early.

title: Court-Ready Estate Accounting from Bank Statements
one_liner: Upload the statements and get the court's accounting format back, so small probate firms stop losing money on the ledger.
customer: Solo and small estate and trust law firms, CPAs acting as fiduciaries, professional fiduciaries, and small trust desks at community banks.
problem: Inventories, receipts-and-disbursements accountings and trust accountings to beneficiaries take 10-30+ hours per estate. Each state and county wants a different format. Small firms bill flat fees or lose money, and errors cause objections and surcharges.
solution: Upload bank and brokerage statements (PDF or CSV). The system categorizes transactions into principal and income, ties to date-of-death balances, flags unusual disbursements, and exports state-format accountings. Start with California plus one more high-volume state (New York or Pennsylvania). A reviewer trail records every override. Later add fiduciary 1041 data and distribution schedules.
why_now: LLM document extraction only recently became reliable on messy statements. Revocable-trust use has grown with online will and trust providers, so more successor trustees face accounting duties.
revenue_model: $149-$399 per accounting or $199-$499/month per firm, with enterprise pricing for banks.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in probate isn't drafting, it's the ledger, and the ledger is what judges and beneficiaries inspect. Whoever owns the estate ledger owns the workflow and the data for tax, inventory and distributions.
first_30_days: Pick California. Recruit 10 small firms through bar section lists. Process 20 accountings manually for $199 each while capturing the county format rules. Publish a sample output for lead generation.

title: Landing Fund: Sweden's Layoff Council for US Employers
one_liner: Employers pay about 0.3% of payroll into a pooled transition fund that gives every laid-off employee case management, retraining money and bridge pay, so companies can restructure without severance drama.
customer: CFOs and CHROs at 200-3,000-employee US companies (software, fintech, insurance, BPO, media) that are restructuring around AI or expect to. Reached through PEOs, HR brokers and benefits consultants.
problem: US severance is ad hoc (about 12-14 weeks for white-collar staff) and outplacement is usually a webinar. Leaders delay or botch layoffs because there is no humane, pre-agreed answer to 'what happens to the people we cut.' One tracker counts roughly 205,000 AI-attributed US layoffs through August 2026, concentrated in entry-level and back-office roles.
solution: A US version of Sweden's Trygghetsrådet (TRR). Employers join a pool at a set percentage of payroll. When someone is laid off they get a named case manager, retraining vouchers, a 2-4 month bridge-pay top-up, and a COBRA/health bridge subsidy, with providers paid partly on outcomes. Employers get a standard offboarding playbook, smaller bespoke severance, and less litigation and survivor-morale damage. Launch as prepaid 'transition credits' (no insurance license needed) and graduate to a captive or reinsured product.
why_now: AI became the top stated reason for corporate job cuts in the spring of 2026, entry-level white-collar hiring has collapsed, and executives are being publicly punished for how they lay people off. In Sweden the model covers 30,000+ companies and about 700,000 employees on 0.3% of payroll, and roughly 9 in 10 active clients found work, study or self-employment within seven months (2019 figures).
revenue_model: Per-employee-per-month or a percentage of payroll (0.2-0.4%). Unspent reserves fund the next cohort, with margin on training-partner rev share and, later, insurance float.
non_obvious_insight: Sweden's system works because employers fund it collectively, so no single firm carries the full cost of a big layoff, and that pooling turns a dreaded cost into a predictable premium. The buyer's real pain is decision speed and reputation, not the money. A ready-made, respected answer to 'what about the people' lets an executive act faster and more humanely, which is why the product can sell before any regulator asks for it.
first_30_days: Build a 'layoff readiness pack' (offboarding checklist, manager scripts, fund terms) and pitch 15 mid-size companies through two PEOs and an HR consultancy. Line up two training providers and one career-coaching group. Target letters of intent from 5-10 founding employers covering about 5,000 employees at roughly $15 per employee per month, with a first paying pool by month 3.

title: Betting Profit-and-Loss Statements for Credit Unions
one_liner: Turn a member's bank ACH data into an 'investment-style' betting P&L (what they recovered per dollar deposited) and optional spending guardrails, licensed per member to credit unions and neobanks.
customer: Community banks, credit unions with young or college-town memberships, and neobanks, paying $0.25-0.60 per member per month. A free consumer version targets Gen Z bettors and their worried parents or partners.
problem: Online betting and prediction-market use is surging among the young. In June-July 2026 first-time users were about 3x January levels. Gen Z and Millennials were 88% of activity (Gen Z 48%). Bettors recovered under 75 cents per dollar sent to platforms. 23% of sports bettors bet daily and 34% weekly. Households that bet had a median deposit balance of only 59% of non-bettors'. Most of these users do not think of themselves as gamblers: 20% of respondents call sports betting a type of investment, Gen Z is about twice as likely to, and buying prediction-market event contracts is more likely to be called an investment than sports betting is.
solution: A detector that classifies ACH and card flows to sportsbooks, sweepstakes casinos and event-contract exchanges, using a maintained list of originator and descriptor names. It produces a plain 'Your realized return: -27%' statement in the vocabulary bettors already use (returns, cost basis), with a monthly summary and opt-in deposit caps or a cooling-off freeze. A parent, partner or co-guardian mode makes it useful for Gen Z members who live at home. The consumer version is a free upload-your-statement tool that generates a shareable 'what's your recovery ratio' card, which doubles as the top of the funnel for credit-union licenses.
why_now: Prediction markets went mainstream in 2026 and the FIFA World Cup drove the June-July spike. Football season, which overlaps other major leagues, starts a new peak now, and first-time users grew 22% YoY in the 2025 football season. Regulators and financial institutions are still working out how to treat event contracts. Under BofA's own framing they sit in a gray zone between entertainment and investing.
revenue_model: B2B: $2-5K/month pilot fees, then $0.25-0.60 per member per month. B2C: free P&L tool, $4.99/month for caps and alerts, and paid family co-guardian seats. Possible later add-on: aggregate, anonymized risk analytics for lenders.
non_obvious_insight: Self-serve gambling blocks fail because bettors do not classify themselves as gamblers, so a harm-reduction message framed as 'gambling addiction' gets ignored, while a return-on-investment statement speaks their mental model. BofA identified betting activity purely from ACH flows, which shows any bank can build the same detection. Working hypothesis, not verified because my search budget ran out: card merchant-category-code blocks used by many banks probably miss ACH-funded prediction-market deposits. Validate with two or three credit-union risk teams before building. Evidence: https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/online-betting-platforms.html and its full PDF https://institute.bankofamerica.com/content/dam/economic-insights/online-betting-platforms.pdf (3x first-timers, recovery under 75 cents, 88% Gen Z plus Millennials, 20% see betting as investing, 59% median balance).
first_30_days: Week 1: compile a list of ACH originator and descriptor names for major sportsbooks, sweepstakes casinos and event-contract exchanges, and ship a client-side upload-a-CSV P&L calculator with a shareable result card. Week 2: seed it in Gen Z finance and sports-betting subreddits and Discords to collect real recovery-ratio numbers. Week 3: cold-email 30 credit unions near universities and military bases (member-financial-wellness and CUSO contacts) with the anonymized ratio data. Week 4: sign one or two paid pilots at $2-5K/month. Legal review of state gambling-related messaging rules is required before launch.
